_meta.indication: TERLIVAZ is indicated to improve kidney function in adults with hepatorenal syndrome with rapid reduction in kidney function.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial comparing IV terlipressin to placebo, with patients randomized 2:1 to terlipressin or placebo.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with cirrhosis, ascites, and hepatorenal syndrome type 1 (HRS-1) with rapidly progressive worsening renal function (SCr ≥ 2.25 mg/dL).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: incidence of Verified HRS Reversal (2 consecutive SCr values ≤ 1.5 mg/dL at least 2 hours apart while on treatment by Day 14 or discharge).
pivotal_trials.n: 300 patients enrolled, randomized 2:1 (TERLIVAZ N=199, placebo N=101).
pivotal_trials.result: Verified HRS Reversal achieved in 58 (29.1%) of TERLIVAZ patients vs 16 (15.8%) placebo patients (p=0.012).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥10%): abdominal pain (19.5% vs 6.1%), nausea (16.0% vs 10.1%), respiratory failure (15.5% vs 7.1%), diarrhea (13.0% vs 7.1%), and dyspnea (12.5% vs 5.1%). Serious or fatal respiratory failure occurred in 14% of TERLIVAZ patients vs 5% on placebo.
target_moa: Terlipressin is a synthetic vasopressin analogue and vasopressin receptor agonist selective for V1 vascular receptors; it acts as a prodrug for lysine-vasopressin and is thought to increase renal blood flow in HRS by reducing portal hypertension.

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: SERIOUS OR FATAL RESPIRATORY FAILURE — TERLIVAZ may cause serious or fatal respiratory failure; patients with volume overload or ACLF Grade 3 are at increased risk; assess oxygen saturation before initiating.

advisory_committee.vote: The Cardiovascular and Renal Drugs Advisory Committee met on July 15, 2020; eight members voted “Yes” and seven members voted “No” on whether terlipressin should be approved for HRS-1.

summary.text: Terlipressin received Orphan Drug designation (October 29, 2004) and Fast-Track designation (April 15, 2005). The NDA was originally submitted in May 2009 and received Complete Response Letters (November 4, 2009; September 11, 2020; February 18, 2022) before regular approval based on the adequate and well-controlled CONFIRM trial. An advisory committee (July 15, 2020) voted 8 Yes to 7 No.

citations.quote: FDA granted Orphan Drug designation and Fast-Track designation on October 29, 2004 and April 15, 2005, respectively.
A U.S. marketing application for terlipressin was originally submitted to FDA for the treatment of HRS-1 in May 2009.
The CONFIRM trial, an adequate and well-controlled trial, demonstrated that terlipressin improves kidney function in adults with HRS with rapid reduction in kidney function
When asked to vote on whether terlipressin should be approved for the treatment of HRS-1, eight Committee members voted “Yes” and seven members voted “No.”

We acknowledge receipt of your amendments dated May 12, 2020, August 19, 2021, and June 9, 2022, which constituted a complete response to our November 4, 2009, September 11, 2020, and February 18, 2022, action letters, respectively.

basis.text: The September 11, 2020 CR letter cited the greater incidence of serious adverse events of respiratory failure with terlipressin versus placebo in CONFIRM and concern that risks might outweigh benefits, with unresolved questions about the clinical significance of the primary endpoint.

citations.quote: On September 11, 2020, the FDA issued a CR letter, citing the greater incidence of serious adverse events (SAEs) of respiratory failure in the terlipressin as compared to the placebo arm in CONFIRM and concern that the risks of terlipressin might outweigh its benefits, particularly given unresolved questions about the clinical significance of the primary endpoint.
